summary: One rule, implemented once in packages/daemon/internal/workflow/adopt.go: a recorded root (Key == Tree) that never ran as a tree of its own (no tree_lifecycles row for its key, no handed_over_roots row) and whose parent is recorded in a live tree (record.TreeLive) is adopted into that tree: it and every record whose Tree is its key are re-recorded with Tree = the live root, Generation+1, LingerUntil/Hold/ReadyPendingVersion cleared, hand-over fence deleted, generation cleared; a todo record enters the run at admitted through enterChild (open gate -> planning), an out-of-workflow record becomes a parked child at phase done that the existing ReenterChild runs on todo; the tree architect gets a child-status notice. Two entry points: admission's sweep at the start of promoteHolds (every admission pass: live events of recorded issues, boot Reconcile, hold release, tick), and release_children through a new intake fact ChildAdoption handled by admission, which refuses (409 CHILD_NOT_ADOPTABLE / CHILD_IN_OTHER_TREE, naming the child and why) before any write and before promote, so the child is in the caller's tree when the release answers. WorkspaceRemove rows gain a Tree fence so the old linger's removal never acts on the adopted child.

tasks.work: Engine.AdoptionRefusal(ctx, tx, issue, tree) (*intake.Refusal, error) and Engine.Adopt(ctx, tx, issue, root, parent) error as the plan's 'The rule' and T1 say; refusal messages name the child key and the reason (ran as a tree of its own; the operator runs a tree under its key; carries a run handed over to it as a root of its own; the tree is not live; runs in the tree of <X>, not <T>).

adoptQueuedRoots(ctx, tx, respectHolds) called first in promoteHolds, fixpoint over todo roots of this project with a recorded parent whose tree root (not itself) is live and not held, AdoptionRefusal nil -> Adopt; non-adoptable roots left as they are; doc comments of Waiting and recordObservation updated.

WorkspaceRemove gains Tree (json tree,omitempty), set at lingerExpired; removeWorkspace finishes without acting when payload.Tree is set and differs from the issue's current tree, and reads the root by payload.Tree; rows without Tree keep today's check.

intake.ChildAdoption{Tree, Children []AdoptedChild{Issue, Parent}}; admission handles it first in applyFact: check every child, return the first refusal before any write and before releaseInactiveSlots/promote; else Adopt each with the Dispatch parent the release read, then promote; Admission.Apply passes the refusal through. waveRelease applies one ChildAdoption for every recorded child outside the grant's tree after validation and before any Dispatch write; enterTodoChild answers a recorded child only when it is in the tree (else 409 CHILD_IN_OTHER_TREE). Comments that say a re-parent leaves the tree as it was are narrowed (architect.go releasableChild, enterTodoChild, owns; notice_routing.go owningArchitect).

Regression tests named in plan.md T5, one or more per acceptance line, D1 and the behaviour changes; API tests wire handlers {engine, admission} with T slotted and an approved gate, and inject the daemon's todo echo themselves (statusRecorder emits no event).

Whole-daemon live proof (-tags e2e) shaped like merged_root_waits_live_test.go / merged-root-waits.sh: steps queued-root-leaves-the-line, release-adopts-from-todo, release-adopts-from-backlog, release-adopts-infra-214-state, release-refuses; membership read from the daemon's Postgres record via record.Store and proven through /legion/v1/children/park answering 200; state read from GET /legion/v1/state.

findings.finding: 1. Roots failing the adoptability gates stay in Waiting and still get a slot, against the spec's no-slot sentence.
findings.answer: Departure D1, accepted by the architect (Envoy c6e46e34d879ac13d3f7ff629a4d07ea): a root with a tree_lifecycles or handed_over_roots row keeps queueing as its own root and release refuses it CHILD_NOT_ADOPTABLE; regression tests TestARootThatRanAsATreeOfItsOwnKeepsQueueingUnderALiveTree and TestACarriedOrphanUnderAReopenedOldRootStillGetsItsSlot.

findings.finding: 2. Observation-time adoption: run the todo child, or only take it out of the queue until release?
findings.answer: Run it (architect accepted, Envoy c6e46e34d879ac13d3f7ff629a4d07ea): it is the existing rule for an unrecorded todo child (workflow/engine.go:316-333, record/project.go:53-54); release_children of an already adopted child answers released with nothing more to do.

findings.finding: 3. Records already in production in the stale state are adopted at the first boot.
findings.answer: Stated in plan.md 'Deploy': the boot sweep adopts only todo never-run roots whose recorded parent is in a live tree. Read 2026-10-26: INFRA-214 is done in Dispatch and its record phase done/status done (read_record), so it is not touched; INFRA-251 is in retro.

findings.finding: 4. 'Child of a live tree': recorded parent vs Dispatch parent chain (unrecorded intermediate parents).
findings.answer: Departure D2, ruled option A by the architect (Envoy 9eac6d833dda5df1f3b1b2935fed19bd): the sweep uses the recorded parent; the unrecorded-intermediate-parent gap is recorded; release_children adopts on its own fresh Dispatch chain read.

findings.finding: 5. The rule also pulls uncarried orphans back into a re-admitted old tree and keeps a queued root under a waiting root inside that root's tree.
findings.answer: Accepted as consequences of TreeLive counting a waiting root as live; tested (TestAnUncarriedOrphanRejoinsItsReadmittedOldTree, TestNestedQueuedRootsJoinTheLiveTreeAtTheTop) and stated in AGENTS.md and the controller's admission reference (T7).

findings.finding: 6. WorkspaceRemove has no generation or tree fence; an old-linger row could remove the adopted child's workspace once the new root lingers at the same generation number.
findings.answer: T3: WorkspaceRemove gains Tree, removeWorkspace finishes without acting when the issue left that tree; daemon outbox test; AC3 tests assert no tree_close/workspace_remove rows after adoption.

findings.finding: 7. Nested/chained stale roots and parent cycles.
findings.answer: The sweep loops to a fixpoint and Adopt carries every record whose Tree is the adopted key; a cycle is broken by the target.Key != issue.Key guard (one of the pair stays waiting); TestNestedQueuedRootsJoinTheLiveTreeAtTheTop.

findings.finding: 8. Reconcile holds: held parent roots; release-path code for holds.
findings.answer: The sweep skips a held candidate and a held target root (respectHolds), adopting at the hold's release (TestAHeldQueuedRootIsAdoptedOnlyOnceTheHoldReleases); the release path ignores holds because it acts on its own fresh Dispatch read, so no new retry code or notice text is needed.

findings.finding: 9. CHILD_IN_OTHER_TREE changes answers for non-roots in another tree; wave half-applied.
findings.answer: In scope as spec line 4 (architect accepted). The wave's adoptions are one ChildAdoption fact that checks every child before any write and returns its refusal before promote; tested in TestReleaseRefusesAChildItCannotAdopt.

findings.finding: 10. Comments and docs that say a re-parent leaves the tree as it was.
findings.answer: T4 narrows api/architect.go (releasableChild, enterTodoChild, owns) and daemon/notice_routing.go comments; T7 updates AGENTS.md, both architect skill copies (claude-envoy regenerated) and the controller admission reference.

findings.finding: 11. API tests wire only {engine}; seeded roots unslotted would be released as unslotted once admission runs.
findings.answer: T5: the new API tests wire {engine, admission}, seed T with a slot and an approved gate, and apply the daemon's todo echo themselves.

findings.finding: 12. Not every admission Apply ends in promote (unrecorded non-todo or unlabelled events return early).
findings.answer: Plan T2 states the entry points precisely and does not rely on an unrecorded parent's own event; a recorded child's re-parent event reaches promote (admit/admit.go:192-200).

findings.finding: 13. leaveUnderOperator is another way to reach todo/phase done.
findings.answer: Its operator lifecycle row makes it non-adoptable; release answers CHILD_NOT_ADOPTABLE with 'the operator runs a tree under its key'; a row of TestReleaseRefusesAChildItCannotAdopt.

findings.finding: 14. Acceptance checks not machine-checkable as written (boot, 'no slot or architect', 'planning starts', 'names the child and why').
findings.answer: plan.md T5/T6 define each: no slots row, no tree_lifecycles row, no architect supervise start for the child, absent from admission.waiting; phase planning plus a planner start row at the new generation; 409 with a fixed code and a message containing the child key and reason phrase; boot covered by TestBootReconcileAdoptsAQueuedRootUnderALiveTree.

specDepartures.spec: Once the daemon sees that a root waiting in its admission queue is now a child of a live tree, the issue leaves the queue and never gets an admission slot or an architect of its own while it is a child of a live tree.
specDepartures.plan: Only a root that never ran as a tree of its own (no tree_lifecycles row, no handed_over_roots row) leaves the queue, by adoption into the tree. A root that ran as a tree of its own (including an operator-held one) or carries a handed-over run keeps queueing as its own root; release_children refuses it 409 CHILD_NOT_ADOPTABLE naming the child and why.
specDepartures.evidence: Taking a carried orphan out of the line would strand a run in progress (its handed-over phase and pull request) with nobody told; AGENTS.md's hand-over contract and packages/daemon/internal/prompts/go/architect-root.md:15 say a handed-over child stays its own tree and reopening its old root does not take it back. Accepted by the architect (Envoy c6e46e34d879ac13d3f7ff629a4d07ea, 2026-10-26T00:04Z), who records it on the issue.

outcome.scope: The queue rule applies to never-run roots; roots that ran or carry a handed-over run keep their own slot. Tested by TestARootThatRanAsATreeOfItsOwnKeepsQueueingUnderALiveTree and TestACarriedOrphanUnderAReopenedOldRootStillGetsItsSlot.

specDepartures.spec: A root waiting in the admission queue that is 'a child of a live tree' leaves the queue.
specDepartures.plan: For the admission sweep, 'child of a live tree' means its recorded parent is recorded in a live tree. A labelled todo issue whose Dispatch parent is not recorded (an unreleased backlog intermediate parent) still queues as its own root, and can take a slot, until that parent is recorded. release_children is not narrowed: it adopts on its own fresh Dispatch chain read.
specDepartures.evidence: Admission does no Dispatch I/O and every fact holds one global lock (admit/admit.go:268-269, intake/facts.go:672-682); the daemon records a child only once todo (workflow/engine.go:316-323). Ruled option A by the architect (Envoy 9eac6d833dda5df1f3b1b2935fed19bd, 2026-10-26T00:10Z): INFRA-214 sat directly under INFRA-168, and a per-ancestor Dispatch read is cost for an edge no one has hit.

outcome.scope: Resolved in this pull request by option B, on the architect's reversal of its option-A ruling (Envoy 495d1feb672177477e891f5fdec91938, 2026-10-26T00:42Z, on the human's standing ruling dispatch://INFRA-49/ask/2d080aec-ce9a-4c7c-a235-ae998d2b0830): the event's preparation and the boot listing read an unrecorded parent's Dispatch chain and carry the nearest recorded ancestor's tree (intake.DispatchIssue.AncestorTree, kept on the record as issues.ancestor_tree); record.Waiting leaves such a root out of the line while that tree is live, so it takes no slot and no architect; release_children of it, or its parent's release and recording, adopts it.
